title: How Can I Enhance My Likeability Among Peers? A quasi-experimental study on self-disclosure in increasing likeability among socially anxious adolescents
abstract: An important need in adolescence is belonging to a social group and being accepted by peers. Adolescents strive to augment their likeability within their social group to fulfill this need. Aim. In the current paper, we sought to extend research on peer likeability ratings among socially anxious adolescents. We proposed self-disclosure as a potential strategy to increase peers’ likeability ratings, especially for socially anxious adolescents. This sample included two groups: "peer rater" (N = 105) and "peer speaker", both pre-screened with the Social Interaction Anxiety Scale (SIAS). Different videos using speakers’ self-disclosure were used to assess their likeability and desire for future interactions. Data were analyzed using ANOVA to examine significant differences in likeability ratings. In line with the adult literature, socially anxious adolescents are prone to receive lower likeability ratings. Findings showed that although socially anxious adolescents tend to receive lower likeability ratings from their peers than non-socially anxious adolescents, self-disclosure may turn these ratings in their favor. Theoretical and clinical implications are discussed.
